Pied-à-terre tax · Statutory Exemptions

Exemptions, LLCs, trusts and combined apartments

Statutory exclusions and primary-residence rules under New York Tax Law Article 30-C (§§ 1350–1356).

Crossing the $1 million condo/co-op threshold or the $5 million house threshold on the assessment roll does not automatically make a property taxable. Under New York Tax Law Article 30-C (§§ 1350–1356), the surcharge applies only to covered residential properties that fail the primary-residence test.

Primary-residence and rental exemptions

As tested on January 5 of the calendar year preceding the fiscal year (January 5, 2026 for FY2027), the surcharge is not owed when the property is the primary residence of:

  • the owner or the owner's spouse;
  • a child, parent, sibling, grandparent, or grandchild of the owner;
  • a tenant or subtenant residing there under a bona fide, arm's-length lease or sublease with a term of at least one year.

LLCs, trusts, and entity ownership

Owning an apartment or townhouse through a limited liability company (LLC) or trust does not by itself qualify a property for an exemption or establish anyone's primary residence. Review the DOF notice determination carefully and consult a New York attorney or CPA on entity documentation.

Statutory exclusions (§ 1351(g)) and other tax abatements (§ 1354(a))

  • Awaiting Certificate of Occupancy (§ 1351(g)(1)): Excludes property still awaiting a required Certificate of Occupancy.
  • Unsold offering-plan units (§ 1351(g)(2)): Excludes units subject to an offering plan where the filer has not yet sold or transferred an economic interest in the unit.
  • No abatement reduction (§ 1354(a)): Standard NYC property tax exemptions and abatements (such as STAR, 421-a, J-51, or the co-op/condo abatement) do not reduce the pied-à-terre surcharge.

Combined apartments across multiple tax lots

The Department of Finance assigns market values lot by lot. If two apartments were physically combined without merging their tax lots, each lot appears separately on the FY2027 roll. The Tax Commission instructs filers to appeal a physically combined home as one residence on Form TC107 (use our free checker to compare adjacent lots).

Residency appeal timing vs. value appeals

The initial 2026–27 direct DOF administrative exemption deadline was October 13, 2026. If you challenged residency with DOF and received a final determination notice, the Tax Commission appeal deadline is the later of March 1 (Class 2) / March 15 (Class 1) or 30 days after that final DOF notice. Market-value protests still face the strict March 1 / March 15 deadline (full calendar).
